claim: Meryem, which originates from Miriam, is a Turkish name.
label: SUPPORTS

gold_evidence.text: It is the Turkish form of [[Maryam_(name)|Maryam]], and is the name used in Turkey to refer to [[Mary_(mother_of_Jesus)|Mary, the mother of Jesus]].
Meriem is another variant form, found as a given name and surname of North African origin.
Maryam or Mariam is the [[Aramaic|Aramaic]] form of the biblical name [[Miriam_(given_name)|Miriam]] (the name of the prophetess [[Miriam|Miriam]], the sister of [[Moses|Moses]]).
It is notably the name of [[Mary_(mother_of_Jesus)|Mary]] the mother of [[Jesus|Jesus]].

The spelling in the [[Semitic_abjad|Semitic abjads]] is mrym (Hebrew מרים, Aramaic ܡܪܝܡ, Arabic مريم), which may be transliterated in a number of ways (Miryam, Miriyam, Mirijam, Marium, Maryam, Mariyam, Marijam, Meryem, Merjeme, etc.)

Via its use in the [[New_Testament|New Testament]] the name has been adopted worldwide, especially in [[Roman_Catholicism|Roman Catholicism]], but also in [[Eastern_Christianity|Eastern Christianity]], in [[Protestantism|Protestantism]], and [[Mary_in_Islam|in Islam]].
In [[Latin_Christianity|Latin Christianity]], the Greek form Mariam was adopted as latinate [[Maria_(given_name)|Maria]] (whence French [[Marie_(given_name)|Marie]] and English [[Mary_(name)|Mary]]).

Forms retaining the final -m are found throughout the Middle East, in [[Arabic|Arabic]], [[Armenian_language|Armenian]], [[Georgian_language|Georgian]], [[Urdu|Urdu]], and [[Persian_language|Persian]], as well as the [[Horn_of_Africa|Horn of Africa]], including Amharic, [[Tigrinya_language|Tigrinya]], and [[Somali_language|Somali]], [[Turkish_language|Turkish]] [[Meryem|Meryem]] and the [[Azerbaijani_language|Azerbaijani]] Məryəm and in [[Malayalam_language|Malayalam]] as Mariyam in south [[India|India]].

The name may have originated from the [[Egyptian_language|Egyptian language]]; in a suggestion going back to 1897, it is possibly derivative of the root mr "love; beloved" (compare [[Meritamen_(given_name)|mry.t-ymn]] "Merit-Amun", i.e. "beloved of [[Amun|Amun]]").
